_comment: Manual overrides per species, keyed by scientific name: {"include": [inat photo ids, forced in first, in this order], "exclude": [inat photo ids never chosen], "description": {"summary", "field_marks", "size", "habitat": text written over the Wikipedia-derived fields}, "limit": N cleared candidates to consider instead of the build's --limit, "trust_article": true to take a Wikipedia article whose lead names neither the BirdNET binomial nor the BirdNET common name, "sounds": {"song": "xc-<nr>", "call": "xc-<nr>" pinned first, "exclude": [recording ids never chosen], "xeno_canto_name": the name xeno-canto files the species under, "accept": [species BirdNET may hear instead, the other half of a split]}}. Photo ids are in the pack's report.json and LICENSE.

Haliaeetus leucocephalus._why: most Bay Area photos are of a distant bird; the first 60 candidates gave one usable crop; a downed juvenile

Passerella iliaca._why: excluded: held in a hand at a banding station

Uria aalge._why: most Bay Area murres on iNaturalist are beached; 200 candidates find live ones; excluded: dead on a beach; beached; dead in the sand; a grounded, sick-looking bird

Regulus satrapa._why: excluded: held in a hand at a banding station

Petrochelidon pyrrhonota._why: excluded: a nestling in the nest

Astur cooperii._why: excluded: a flock, not a Cooper's Hawk

Numenius hudsonicus._why: BirdNET+ carries both halves of the whimbrel split and hears American recordings as Numenius phaeopus (#41: six xeno-canto and two iNaturalist clips refused that way)

Setophaga aestiva._why: BirdNET+ carries both halves of the yellow warbler split and hears American recordings as Setophaga petechia (#41)

Larus brachyrhynchus._why: BirdNET+ carries both halves of the mew gull split and hears American recordings as Larus canus (#41: five xeno-canto clips refused that way)
